value.body: Researches companies, sectors and the economy to support decisions on buying, holding or selling investments. Employers include mutual funds, portfolio-management and broking firms, investment banks, insurers and research outsourcing firms. A typical day involves reading results and filings, updating financial models and writing notes for fund managers or clients.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com, BBA or B.Sc, often followed by an MBA (Finance), CA or CFA

items.label: Regulatory certificate
items.note: Needed for SEBI-registered research analyst roles

items.label: SEBI-registered research analysts
items.note: Up from ~620 in 2018-19; many analysts work inside registered firms rather than registering individually
items.source: SEBI data (as reported by Business Standard)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often begin as junior or associate analysts at research outsourcing firms or brokerages, updating models and data for senior analysts. Accounting knowledge, Excel modelling and clear writing are tested, often through a case study. CFA Level I or an MBA (Finance) is common among applicants, and the NISM research-analyst certificate is required for certain SEBI-regulated roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading financial statements and annual reports

value.title: At a glance
items: Competition for fund-side roles is high; many start in research support and move up.
Growth path: associate → analyst → senior analyst or portfolio manager.
Results seasons and market events bring busy periods.

competition.note: B.Com graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
